_comment: Width-conversion rules for wires landing on vector fields.
(which only pins that the TS `WireConvert` union names the same modes -- there
is no TS executor twin to replay the math against, since the web runs the same
`comps` entries are null where the wire drives nothing: that lane keeps
whatever the consumer already had (its authored value, or an earlier wire's
fold). That is the whole point of the lane mask, so the nulls are assertions,
srcLane/destLane default to -1 (the whole field); convert defaults to auto.

cases.name: auto: a scalar broadcasts to every lane
auto: a scalar broadcasts across a float3
auto: equal widths are elementwise
auto: rgba into rgb drops alpha
auto: rgb into rgba leaves the authored alpha alone
auto: a vec into a scalar field takes component 0
auto: a dormant rail drives nothing
broadcast: component 0 drives every lane
broadcast: widens a scalar to float4
truncate: a scalar drives lane 0 alone (the anti-broadcast)
truncate: rgb into rgba still leaves alpha undriven
truncate: nothing to drop when the source is wider
pad: rgb into rgba fills alpha from the declared default
pad: a scalar fills the rest from declared defaults
pad: missing declared defaults read as zero
pad: a wider source has nothing left to pad
srcLane: picks one component of a vec source
srcLane: the picked component then broadcasts
srcLane: out of range is ignored, not fatal
destLane: a scalar drives only the addressed lane
destLane: a wide source reduces to component 0
destLane: out of range falls back to the width rule
destLane: beats convert, which has nothing left to decide
destLane: a dormant rail drives nothing
srcLane and destLane compose
